title: Forces and free-body diagrams; Newton's first law and equilibrium
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics 1 (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: D01-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; D01-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; D01-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; D02-1#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: D01-1#N.6b, D02-1#N.2, D01-1#N.12, D02-1#N.4, D01-1#N.14, D02-1#N.11.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Mass
items.clue: Amount of matter in an object, in kg; the same everywhere.

items.label: Tension
items.clue: Pull of a string, rope or cable, acting along it and away from the object.

items.label: Friction
items.clue: Force parallel to a surface that opposes sliding, or the tendency to slide.

items.label: Equilibrium
items.clue: State of a body, such as a steadily falling skydiver, whose forces balance.

questions.stem: A rover weighs 1600 N at Earth's surface. Use g = 10 m s⁻². The gravitational field strength at the surface of Mars is 3.7 N kg⁻¹. What is the rover's weight on Mars?
questions.explanation: The rover's mass is the same everywhere: m = W/g = 1600 N ÷ 10 N/kg = 160 kg. On Mars its weight is 160 kg × 3.7 N/kg = 592 N ≈ 5.9 × 10² N.

questions.stem: A space probe is so far from any star or planet that the forces exerted on it are negligible. Its engines fire briefly and then shut off. Which statement describes the probe's motion after the engines have shut off?

options.text: It slows down and stops, as all moving objects do in time.
It slows down as the force from the engine firing is used up.
It moves in a straight line at a constant speed.
It stops almost at once, as no force now pushes it forward.

questions.stem: A crate is given a push and then slides down a rough ramp on its own. Which list gives all the forces acting on the crate while it slides, and no others?

options.text: Weight, normal force, friction up the ramp and a force of motion down the ramp
Weight, normal force and friction down the ramp
Weight, normal force from the ramp and friction up the ramp
Weight, a separate force down the slope, normal force and friction

questions.explanation: Earth pulls down; the ramp pushes perpendicular to its surface and, as the crate slides down it, rubs back up it. Three forces, each with a source.

questions.stem: A puck slides east at constant velocity across level ice with negligible friction. Starting at time t, a constant force directed north is exerted on the puck, and no other horizontal force acts. Which statement describes the puck's motion after time t?

options.text: It turns and moves due north, in the direction of the force on it.
Its eastward velocity decreases while its northward velocity increases.
It moves at a constant velocity in a direction between east and north.
Its eastward velocity stays the same while its northward velocity increases.

questions.stem: A hockey puck is hit by a stick and then slides across level ice. Friction and air resistance are negligible. Which forces are exerted on the puck while it slides, after it has left the stick?

options.text: Earth's pull, the ice's push and a fading push left over from the hit
A downward pull by Earth and an upward push by the ice that touches it
A downward pull by Earth, and no force at all from the ice
An upward push by the ice, with no gravitational force on a supported puck

questions.stem: Which of the following objects is in translational equilibrium?

options.text: A ball at the top of its flight, momentarily at rest
A car rounding a curve on a level road at a constant speed
A puck slowing down on rough ice after a stick stops pushing it
A crate riding up a straight conveyor at a steady 2 m s⁻¹

questions.explanation: Its speed and direction are both constant, so its velocity is constant and the net force on it is zero: friction from the belt, up the slope, balances the component of its weight down the slope, and the normal force balances the rest.
